confidence_notes: I used three of the six allowed web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Palermo prices. Restaurant meal, cappuccino and draft beer anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living sources (crowdsourced or modelled, dated 2023-2026). They have been nudged upward for July 2026 summer peak and tourist-area pricing. The inexpensive meal is set above the lowest aggregated figures (about USD 8.50-14) to reflect a sit-down tourist-area trattoria. Euros were converted to USD using a EUR/USD cross rate of about 1.10, implied by the RBA AUD rates (0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR). Cocktail and wine prices are less certain. They come from a 2026 Palermo nightlife guide and a user review (spritz about EUR 5-9, cocktails about EUR 6-10, wine EUR 5-7 a glass), not from aggregated indexes, and were checked against the local beer price. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge only, with no booking or listing searches. They assume July high season with demand from Sicilian beach tourism, so actual rates could vary by about ±25% depending on location (centro storico vs outskirts) and dates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are benchmarked to southern Italian cities such as Naples, Catania and Bari. Sources put Palermo about 7-8% below the Italian average for food and drink, with summer accommodation premiums typical of Mediterranean coastal destinations.
